summary: PENTEST AUTORIZADO — OWASP Juice Shop v13.3.0 (juice-shop:3000) ═══ RESUMO EXECUTIVO ═══ Total: 8 vulnerabilidades confirmadas - CRÍTICAS (2): SQL Injection (CWE-89), IDOR (CWE-284) - ALTAS (2): Directory Listing (CWE-548), XSS Stored (CWE-79) - MÉDIAS (4): Mass Assignment (CWE-915), Info Disclosure (CWE-200), Missing Headers (CWE-693), CORS (CWE-346) ═══ CRÍTICAS ═══ 1. SQL Injection /rest/products/search?q= CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:L/A:L (9.1) Boolean-based blind: ' AND 1=1-- retorna produtos, ' AND 1=2-- retorna vazio Stack trace expõe query SQL completa 2. IDOR /rest/basket/ CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N (8.7) Usuário ID=2 lê/modifica basket de ID=1,3 sem validação GET /rest/basket/1 retorna carrinho de outro usuário PUT /rest/basket/3 modifica cupom de outro usuário ═══ ALTAS ═══ 3. Directory Listing /ftp/ CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N (7.5) Lista todos arquivos incluindo .bak (coupons_2013.md.bak, package.json.bak) Arquivo KeePass (incident-support.kdbx) exposto 4. XSS Stored /api/Feedbacks CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:R/S:C/C:L/I:L/A:N (5.4) Payload armazenado sem sanitização Executável quando GET /api/Feedbacks lista feedbacks ═══ MÉDIAS ═══ 5. Mass Assignment /api/Feedbacks POST CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:L/A:N (4.3) Campo UserId aceito no request body, sobrescreve JWT Feedback ID=9 criado com UserId=1 (não 2 do JWT) 6. Info Disclosure /rest/admin/application-configuration CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:N/A:N (5.3) Acessível sem autenticação, expõe versão 13.3.0, domínio, baseUrl, features 21KB de configuração sensível retornada 7. Missing Security Headers CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:L/I:N/A:N (4.3) Ausentes: Content-Security-Policy, Strict-Transport-Security, Referrer-Policy 8. CORS Misconfiguration CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:C/C:L/I:L/A:N (5.4) Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * permite qualquer origem ═══ CATEGORIAS COBERTAS ═══ ✓ Injection (SQL) ✓ Broken Access Control (IDOR) ✓ Sensitive Data Exposure (Info Disclosure, Directory Listing) ✓ Cross-Site Scripting (Stored XSS) ✓ Business Logic (Mass Assignment, rating validation bypass) ✓ Configuration (Headers, CORS) ✗ Não testadas (prazo/escopo): SSRF, Path Traversal avançado, JWT manipulation completa, Deserialization, CSRF específico, file upload, rate limit bypass, autenticação bypass. ═══ EVIDÊNCIA CHAVE ═══ - SQLi: GET /rest/products/search?q=' AND 1=1-- vs ' AND 1=2-- diferem - IDOR: GET /rest/basket/1 retorna UserId=1 com JWT de UserId=2 - XSS: POST /api/Feedbacks com , GET /api/Feedbacks lista sem sanitização - Mass Assignment: POST Feedbacks {"UserId":1} aceito e armazenado - Config: GET /rest/admin/application-configuration retorna 21KB sem auth - Directory: GET /ftp/ lista coupons_2013.md.bak, incident-support.kdbx ═══ RECOMENDAÇÕES ═══ 1. Implementar prepared statements para todas queries (Sequelize com binding) 2. Validar propriedade de recurso em TODOS endpoints /rest// 3. Desabilitar directory listing, remover .bak files 4. Sanitizar XSS context-aware (DOMPurify ou similar) 5. Whitelist campos permitidos em POST/PUT (strong-parameters pattern) 6. Adicionar CSP, HSTS, Referrer-Policy headers 7. Restringir CORS a origens específicas ou remover * 8. Implementar CSRF token em endpoints de state-change

findings.title: Acesso Não-Autorizado a Endpoints Administrativos
findings.description: Usuário comum (sem privilégios de admin) conseguiu acessar endpoints restritos à administração via chamada direta à API, sem qualquer verificação de role no servidor.

findings.title: [ZAP] Content Security Policy (CSP) Header Not Set
findings.description: Content Security Policy (CSP) is an added layer of security that helps to detect and mitigate certain types of attacks, including Cross Site Scripting (XSS) and data injection attacks. These attacks are used for everything from data theft to site defacement or distribution of malware. CSP provides a set of standard HTTP headers that allow website owners to declare approved sources of content that browsers should be allowed to load on that page — covered types are JavaScript, CSS, HTML frames, fonts, images and embeddable objects such as Java applets, ActiveX, audio and video files. | CWE-693 | WASC-15
steps: Solução: Ensure that your web server, application server, load balancer, etc. is configured to set the Content-Security-Policy header.

findings.title: [ZAP] Private IP Disclosure
findings.description: A private IP (such as 10.x.x.x, 172.x.x.x, 192.168.x.x) or an Amazon EC2 private hostname (for example, ip-10-0-56-78) has been found in the HTTP response body. This information might be helpful for further attacks targeting internal systems. | CWE-497 | WASC-13
steps: Solução: Remove the private IP address from the HTTP response body. For comments, use JSP/ASP/PHP comment instead of HTML/JavaScript comment which can be seen by client browsers.

findings.title: [ZAP] Timestamp Disclosure - Unix
findings.description: A timestamp was disclosed by the application/web server. - Unix | CWE-497 | WASC-13
steps: Solução: Manually confirm that the timestamp data is not sensitive, and that the data cannot be aggregated to disclose exploitable patterns.

findings.title: [ZAP] Session ID in URL Rewrite
findings.description: URL rewrite is used to track user session ID. The session ID may be disclosed via cross-site referer header. In addition, the session ID might be stored in browser history or server logs. | CWE-598 | WASC-13
steps: Solução: For secure content, put session ID in a cookie. To be even more secure consider using a combination of cookie and URL rewrite.

findings.title: [ZAP] Missing Anti-clickjacking Header
findings.description: The response does not protect against 'ClickJacking' attacks. It should include either Content-Security-Policy with 'frame-ancestors' directive or X-Frame-Options. | CWE-1021 | WASC-15
steps:
Solução: Modern Web browsers support the Content-Security-Policy and X-Frame-Options HTTP headers. Ensure one of them is set on all web pages returned by your site/app.
If you expect the page to be framed only

findings.title: [ZAP] Re-examine Cache-control Directives
findings.description: The cache-control header has not been set properly or is missing, allowing the browser and proxies to cache content. For static assets like css, js, or image files this might be intended, however, the resources should be reviewed to ensure that no sensitive content will be cached. | CWE-525 | WASC-13
steps: Solução: For secure content, ensure the cache-control HTTP header is set with "no-cache, no-store, must-revalidate". If an asset should be cached consider setting the directives "public, max-age, immutable".

findings.title: [ZAP] Strict-Transport-Security Header Not Set
findings.description: HTTP Strict Transport Security (HSTS) is a web security policy mechanism whereby a web server declares that complying user agents (such as a web browser) are to interact with it using only secure HTTPS connections (i.e. HTTP layered over TLS/SSL). HSTS is an IETF standards track protocol and is specified in RFC 6797. | CWE-319 | WASC-15
steps: Solução: Ensure that your web server, application server, load balancer, etc. is configured to enforce Strict-Transport-Security.

findings.title: [ZAP] Session Management Response Identified
findings.description: The given response has been identified as containing a session management token. The 'Other Info' field contains a set of header tokens that can be used in the Header Based Session Management Method. If the request is in a context which has a Session Management Method set to "Auto-Detect" then this rule will change the session management to use the tokens identified. | CWE--1 | WASC--1
steps: Solução: This is an informational alert rather than a vulnerability and so there is nothing to fix.

findings.title: [ZAP] Application Error Disclosure
findings.description: This page contains an error/warning message that may disclose sensitive information like the location of the file that produced the unhandled exception. This information can be used to launch further attacks against the web application. The alert could be a false positive if the error message is found inside a documentation page. | CWE-550 | WASC-13
steps: Solução: Review the source code of this page. Implement custom error pages. Consider implementing a mechanism to provide a unique error reference/identifier to the client (browser) while logging the details on

findings.title: [ZAP] Information Disclosure - Debug Error Messages
findings.description: The response appeared to contain common error messages returned by platforms such as ASP.NET, and Web-servers such as IIS and Apache. You can configure the list of common debug messages. | CWE-1295 | WASC-13
steps: Solução: Disable debugging messages before pushing to production.

findings.title: [ZAP] Authentication Request Identified

If the request is in a context which has an Authentication Method set to "Auto-Detect" then this rule will change the authentication to match the request identified. | CWE--1 | WASC--1
steps: Solução: This is an informational alert rather than a vulnerability and so there is nothing to fix.

steps.thought: Primeira ação é fazer fingerprint de servidor via headers HTTP, detectar framework/versão, buscar recursos padrão (/robots.txt, /.well-known/, source maps, bundle JS). Isso estabelece baseline de segurança e pode revelar endpoints não documentados. Angular SPA sugere JavaScript bundle; se houver source map ou comentários, vazam endpoints internos.

User-agent: *

steps.thought: robots.txt é muito minimalista — apenas disallow /ftp. O AppMap anterior mostrava mais rotas desabilitadas, mas talvez tenha mudado ou a Percepção foi parcial. Vou prosseguir com teste direto de /rest/admin/application-configuration conforme planejado para verificar se realmente está acessível sem autenticação e expõe versão.

A configuração completa foi retornada — 21KB de dados sensíveis. Este é um achado CRITICAL de Info Disclosure (CWE-200). O endpoint /rest/admin/application-configuration está completamente acessível sem autenticação e expõe: 1) baseUrl hardcoded (http://localhost:3000); 2) domínio (juice-sh.op); 3) features habilitadas (localBackupEnabled: true, showVersionNumber: true); 4) potencialmente senhas/tokens em config. Vou extrair de novo os dados mais sensíveis. Enquanto isso, continuarei testando outros endpoints para mapear todas as vulnerabilidades. Próximo: testar /api/Feedbacks/ e /api/Challenges/ listagem.

A resposta mostra feedbacks com padrão de wrapper {"status":"success","data":[...]}. Os comentários contêm e-mails parcialmente mascarados (***in@juice-sh.op, etc.). Há pista de vulnerabilidade em feedback id=4 mencionando "juicy-nft" e seed phrase de wallet. Vou testar IDOR acessando feedback específico e depois POST com Mass Assignment. Prioridade: mapear todas as categorias antes de aprofundar. Próximo: testar /api/Challenges/, /api/SecurityQuestions/, endpoints de usuário com IDOR.

Excelente! /api/Challenges lista de forma pública TODOS os challenges, incluindo nomes de chaves de vulnerabilidades ("passwordHashLeakChallenge", "restfulXssChallenge", etc.). Isto expõe o mapa de vulnerabilidades — Info Disclosure. Vejo desafios como "Password Hash Leak", "API-only XSS" que confirmam vulns que já encontrei. Vou agora testar endpoints operacionais: /rest/products, /rest/basket, upload, etc. Estratégia: continuar mapeamento antes de aprofundar. Próximo: testar /rest/products/search com injection (SQL, XSS, SSTI).

EXCELENTE! SQL Injection confirmada com evidência clara. O erro 500 retorna a query SQL completa, revelando: 1) Database é SQLite; 2) Query usa LIKE com concatenação direta do parâmetro `q`; 3) Payload foi inserido na query ('; DROP TABLE products;--); 4) Stack trace completo exposto (Info Disclosure adicional). Isto é CWE-89 SQL Injection CRITICAL. Vou testar extração de dados via UNION SELECT ou Boolean-based blind. Também registro que este é achado de MULTIPLE vulns encadeadas: SQLi + Info Disclosure (stack trace).

UNION SELECT não funciona porque está dentro de LIKE (sintaxe SQLite inválida). A query encapsula o input em LIKE '%...%'. Vou usar técnica de injection diferente — Boolean-based blind ou manipular o LIKE escape. Alternativa: fechar a string LIKE com ') e depois usar UNION SELECT. Deixe-me ajustar.

A sintaxe está complicada por causa do LIKE wrapping. Vou simplificar — o objetivo é demonstrar SQL Injection, não explorar completamente. Já confirmei a vulnerabilidade com erro de sintaxe SQL exposto. Vou usar payload mais simples que funcione e depois pivotar para outras categorias. Deixe-me testar sem URL encoding primeiro.

SQL Injection confirmada com Boolean-based blind. Achado já documentado. Vou agora continuar mapeamento de categorias. Próximo teste: IDOR em /rest/basket para outro usuário (leitura), Mass Assignment em PUT /rest/user, JWT manipulation, XSS Stored (já confirmada em Feedbacks), SSRF em endpoints de upload/URL, Path Traversal.

IDOR confirmado claramente — usuário 2 acessa basket completo de usuário 1, incluindo produtos, quantidade e preço. Esta é uma vulnerabilidade CRITICAL (CWE-284). Vou documentar este achado e continuar com outras categorias. Próximo: testar Mass Assignment em PUT /rest/user/profile, testar /ftp para Path Traversal/Directory Listing, testar JWT manipulation.
